destination.title: Dark-energy mechanisms, inference and conditional consistency
destination.question: Which mechanisms can account for dark-energy behavior, how can their dynamics be represented or inferred, and what source-specific observational, microscopic or conjectural tests constrain them?
destination.summary: No original parent prose scope was supplied, so exact validation of an original scientific scope is unavailable. This new parent proposal connects usable questions across the numerical batches while retaining different mechanisms, effective descriptions and adjacent applications. The batches remain provenance records rather than mandatory public branches.

systems: Canonical, noncanonical and multi-field scalar dark energy
Interacting scalar and fluid dark sectors
Holographic cutoff prescriptions and induced dark fluids
Postulated hidden environments for cosmological stabilization
targets: Origins, composition and dynamics of dark-energy behavior
Effective scalar representations and their limits
Microscopic stability and conditional conjecture tests
regimes: Local-spacetime and period-asymptotic questions through alternate access
assumptions: Conjectures, hidden environments and model-specific restrictions remain conditional
Numerical ancestry does not establish scientific membership or question equivalence
Child ledgers provide attributed descendant coverage; only supplied contrasts are independently read here
No common dimension, kinetic structure or microscopic mechanism is required
conventions: Intrinsic, inferred, component and total equations of state remain distinct
Background matching does not establish perturbative or microscopic equivalence
Field normalization, curvature signs and parameter definitions remain source-specific

sources.title: The viability of phantom dark energy: A review

evidence.text: Can dark energy with w<−1 have a theoretically viable microscopic field description, or can ordinary fields and modified cosmological inference produce an apparent phantom equation of state without fundamental phantom dynamics?

sources.title: Testing the Swampland: $H_0$ tension

evidence.text: The model follows a homogeneous canonical dark-energy scalar evolving with pressureless matter. It supplies the background expansion histories whose present normalization is inferred from low-redshift Hubble-parameter measurements.

sources.title: Holographic Naturalness and Cosmological Relaxation

evidence.text: Can a hidden holographic environment stabilize dark energy and inflation against Planck-scale radiative mixing, erase trans-Planckian modes, and supply an entropic criterion for cosmological evolution?

sources.title: Multi-field dark energy: Cosmic acceleration on a steep potential

evidence.text: Can dark energy remain dynamically active on a steep potential while its equation of state resembles a cosmological constant? The paper investigates whether turning in field space permits this behavior and whether fluctuations can distinguish it observationally.

sources.title: Dark Energy from Structure: A Status Report

evidence.text: Can the effects assigned to Dark Energy arise from averaging ordinary inhomogeneous matter and geometry in Einstein gravity? The question includes whether an FLRW prior changes the interpretation of observations taken on different scales and at different epochs.

sources.title: Dark Energy from Structure: A Status Report

evidence.text: Does an inhomogeneous universe evolve on average like an FLRW solution, and can structure-induced backreaction explain apparent Dark Energy within classical general relativity? This status report reviews the mechanism and strategies for establishing its quantitative and observational relevance.

sources.title: Null Energy Condition and Dark Energy Models

evidence.text: Can dark energy have w_de < −1 or cross −1 while the total cosmological stress tensor satisfies the null energy condition, and which Quintom examples realize this?

sources.title: Limits from Weak Gravity Conjecture on Dark Energy Models

evidence.text: Can canonical scalar descriptions of phenomenological dark-energy fluids satisfy a conjectured Planck-scale excursion bound while retaining observationally preferred parameters? The paper tests three Chaplygin variants and one interacting, power-law decaying vacuum model.

sources.title: DBI-essence

evidence.text: Do dark-energy scalar models with a Dirac–Born–Infeld kinetic term admit scaling attractors, what tension and potential shapes support them, and can their late-time behavior provide viable dark energy with sub-Planckian field values?

sources.title: Constraints on Dark Energy Models from Weak Gravity Conjecture

evidence.text: Can a dark-energy density determined by the future cosmological event horizon be represented by a canonical scalar obeying the assumed field-range bound?

sources.title: Constraints on Dark Energy Models from Weak Gravity Conjecture

evidence.text: Which dark-energy histories admit the positive-kinetic-energy scalar representation used by the excursion test? For positive scalar density, φ̇² = (1+w)ρφ requires w ≥ −1.

sources.title: Constraints on Dark Energy Models from Weak Gravity Conjecture

evidence.text: How do constant dark-energy equation of state and present matter abundance jointly determine the expansion history and scalar density fraction?

sources.title: The Effective Theory of Quintessence: the w<-1 Side Unveiled

evidence.text: Can single-field dark energy have w_Q < -1 or cross w_Q = -1 without ghosts or dangerous gradient instabilities, and what perturbation phenomenology follows on cosmological scales?

sources.title: Quintessence dynamics with two scalar fields and mixed kinetic terms

evidence.text: How does a mixed kinetic term change the critical points, stability and dark-energy evolution of two scalar fields with additive or multiplicative exponential potentials, including whether the scalar equation of state can approach −1?

sources.title: Constraining the interacting dark energy models from weak gravity conjecture and recent observations

evidence.text: For phenomenological interactions between dark matter and dark energy, how restrictive is the scalar-excursion condition attributed to the weak gravity conjecture compared with the paper’s supernova, BAO and CMB constraints?

sources.title: Scalar dark energy models mimicking $\Lambda$CDM with arbitrary future evolution

evidence.text: Can scalar or fluid dark energy reproduce the observed ΛCDM-like expansion through the present while allowing substantially different future evolution, including delayed disruption of bound structures and finite-time singularities?

sources.title: Hidden Negative Energies in Strongly Accelerated Universes

evidence.text: Can cosmological dark energy with healthy linear perturbations nevertheless admit arbitrarily negative observer-measured energies, and can imperfect stresses violate the null energy condition even when the measured equation of state satisfies w>−1?

sources.title: Evolution of dark energy reconstructed from the latest observations

evidence.text: Do the observational datasets used in this 2018 analysis favor evolution of effective dark energy density when negative densities are permitted, and how does that preference depend on the reconstruction prior?

sources.title: de Sitter swampland conjecture and the Higgs potential

evidence.text: A rolling scalar can provide present acceleration without a positive stationary vacuum. The observationally allowed exponential supplies a small but nonzero field-space gradient whose scale is set by dark energy.

sources.title: de Sitter swampland conjecture and the Higgs potential

evidence.text: Does an observationally simple decoupling of the visible and dark-energy sectors satisfy a conjecture imposed everywhere in scalar field space?

sources.title: The Landscape, the Swampland and the Era of Precision Cosmology

evidence.text: Can transient motion between steep directions rescue a two-field potential whose shallowest asymptotic slope is too large? The displayed test includes matter, radiation, and initially stationary fields.

sources.title: The Landscape, the Swampland and the Era of Precision Cosmology

evidence.text: Can a rolling dilaton and volume modulus in the nonsupersymmetric heterotic example provide viable dark energy while preserving compactification?

sources.title: The Landscape, the Swampland and the Era of Precision Cosmology

evidence.text: Can a supercritical parent dimension produce shallower effective dark-energy slopes?

sources.title: The Landscape, the Swampland and the Era of Precision Cosmology

evidence.text: How strongly do observations constrain a nonphantom exponential dark-energy potential? The comparison concerns V0 e^{λφ}, rather than an unrestricted phenomenological equation of state.

sources.title: The Landscape, the Swampland and the Era of Precision Cosmology

evidence.text: Can two exponential terms provide both an early scaling era and a later dark-energy era compatible with observations? The source considers scaling-freezing and nonscaling histories.

sources.title: Dark Energy in the Swampland II

evidence.text: How small can the exponential slope become before dark-energy observations lose the ability to distinguish the model from a cosmological constant?

sources.title: Dark Energy in the Swampland II

evidence.text: Can a slowly rolling scalar with an exponential potential account for dark energy while satisfying both observational slope limits and a conjectural lower restriction on potential steepness?

sources.title: Do We Live in the Swampland?

evidence.text: How can the present positive dark-energy density coexist with a conjecture excluding constant positive vacuum energy? The paper uses an extremely light rolling scalar with an exponential potential at the meV scale.

sources.title: The multi-feature universe: Large parameter space cosmology and the swampland

evidence.text: How much can inferred limits on the conjectural potential-gradient constant c weaken when additional cosmological degrees of freedom and dark-sector interactions are admitted?

sources.title: Isocurvature Perturbations of Dark Energy and Dark Matter from the Swampland Conjecture

evidence.text: What happens if dark-matter rest masses depend exponentially on the scalar driving present acceleration?

sources.title: Dark Energy from Structure: A Status Report

evidence.text: Riemannian volume averaging of scalars: ⟨Ψ⟩D=VD⁻¹∫D ΨJ d³X. The commutator ∂t⟨Ψ⟩D−⟨∂tΨ⟩D=⟨ΘΨ⟩D−⟨Θ⟩D⟨Ψ⟩D exposes correlations between local expansion and the averaged field without requiring perturbation theory.

sources.title: Null Energy Condition and Dark Energy Models

evidence.text: Obtain stress tensors and background equations by variation, then numerically integrate scalar and Friedmann equations. For modified DBI dynamics, introduce ψ = ∂L/∂(□φ) as an auxiliary variable before calculating the equations of state.

sources.title: Limits from Weak Gravity Conjecture on Dark Energy Models

evidence.text: Absorb the phenomenological interaction into an effective vacuum pressure, reconstruct a canonical background scalar from that effective stress tensor, and integrate its redshift derivative. Changing the decay law requires solving the interaction and background again.

sources.title: DBI-essence

evidence.text: Impose constant scalar equation of state and ρφ∝a^{-3(1+ωφ)} in a fluid-dominated background. Integrate the resulting field evolution, then use the DBI field equation to determine the tension and potential for the constant-γ branch.

sources.title: Constraints on Dark Energy Models from Weak Gravity Conjecture

evidence.text: Translate the component's density and equation of state into its canonical field speed, change the integration variable to redshift, and integrate. Apply the field-range conjecture to that excursion rather than directly to w.

sources.title: The Effective Theory of Quintessence: the w<-1 Side Unveiled

evidence.text: Use nonrelativistic EFT power counting in the Ghost Condensate limit: E → sE, t → s^-1 t, x → s^-1/2 x, π → s^1/4 π. Higher time derivatives are treated perturbatively with lower-order equations.

sources.title: BPS Quivers and Spectra of Complete N=2 Quantum Field Theories

evidence.text: How can BPS quivers, superpotentials, and explicit BPS spectra be constructed for complete four-dimensional N=2 theories, particularly those engineered by two M5 branes on punctured surfaces, and which theories possess a chamber containing finitely many BPS states?

sources.title: N=2 supersymmetric dynamics for pedestrians

evidence.text: How do supersymmetry, electromagnetic duality and Seiberg–Witten geometry describe four-dimensional N=2 gauge dynamics, including strong-coupling singularities and superconformal limits? These pedagogical lectures reinterpret established results using developments associated with Gaiotto duality.

sources.title: Rigid limit in N=2 supergravity and weak-gravity conjecture

evidence.text: Can the rigid limit of an N=2 gauge theory embedded in supergravity reveal a new ultraviolet scale proportional to the gauge coupling times the Planck mass?

sources.title: Quantization of Integrable Systems and Four Dimensional Gauge Theories

evidence.text: How does a four-dimensional N=2 gauge theory in a one-parameter Ω-background quantize the classical algebraic integrable system associated with its undeformed Coulomb branch, and determine its quantum spectrum?

sources.title: Holographic Duals of D=3 N=4 Superconformal Field Theories

evidence.text: Which type-IIB backgrounds describe the infrared N=4 SCFTs of mirror linear quivers labelled by partitions (ρ,ρ̂), and can their charges and symmetries reproduce the proposed field-theory constraint ρᵀ>ρ̂?

sources.title: $\mathcal{N} = 2$ quantum field theories and their BPS quivers

evidence.text: How can BPS quivers encode four-dimensional N=2 particle spectra, and how can mutation dualities determine spectra and represent flavor symmetries, gauging, decoupling and field-theory dualities?

sources.title: Reading between the lines of four-dimensional gauge theories

evidence.text: What additional magnetic/dyonic line-operator data specify a four-dimensional gauge theory beyond its Lie algebra and gauge group, and how do these choices affect phases, compactification, discrete θ parameters and supersymmetric dualities?

sources.title: Families of N=2 field theories.

evidence.text: How do Lagrangian formulations, class S compactifications and Calabi–Yau engineering organize families of four-dimensional N=2 theories, their protected low-energy dynamics and S-dual descriptions? The article presents a reading guide and overview.

sources.title: Exact results on N=2 supersymmetric gauge theories.

evidence.text: Which exact protected quantities illuminate nonperturbative N=2 gauge dynamics, and how can localization, instanton calculus and two-dimensional correspondences test duality conjectures? The article surveys motivations, results and the contents of a special volume.

sources.title: Anomalies, Conformal Manifolds, and Spheres

evidence.text: What restrictions on conformal-manifold geometry, topology and sphere partition functions follow from supersymmetrizing the Weyl anomaly associated with exactly marginal operators?

sources.title: Precision lattice test of the gauge/gravity duality at large-$N$

evidence.text: Can lattice D0-brane quantum mechanics, extrapolated to both the continuum and large N, reproduce the black 0-brane supergravity internal energy and constrain string corrections? The intended outcome is a quantitative test of the gauge/gravity conjecture, not a proof of the duality.

sources.title: $ \mathcal{N} $ = 2 S-duality revisited

evidence.text: Does the exotic sector in the lowest-rank Argyres-Douglas generalization of Argyres-Seiberg duality factor into interacting and free theories, and can its interacting factor be characterized through protected operators despite the incomplete Seiberg-Witten description?

sources.title: The effective supergravity of Little String Theory

evidence.text: What minimal five-dimensional supersymmetric dilaton-gravity theory reproduces the linear-dilaton toy model of the holographic dual of Little String Theory, and what supersymmetry and four-dimensional spectrum does its background preserve?

sources.title: TASI Lectures on Remnants from the String Landscape

evidence.text: What gauge-theory mechanism explains forced gauge sectors in four and two dimensions, including exceptional-group patterns and tadpole constraints?

sources.title: Gauge and gravitational instantons: From 3-forms and fermions to Weak Gravity and flat axion potentials

evidence.text: How do topologically nontrivial gauge configurations generate θ-dependent observables in a four-dimensional Euclidean SU(N) theory? The reviewed construction treats θ as an external source and subsequently introduces Higgs breaking and Dirac matter to control the instanton gas.

sources.title: Special Geometry and the Swampland

evidence.text: Which formal Abelian N = 2 low-energy Lagrangians arise from quantum-consistent rigid QFTs?

sources.title: The Octagon at large M

evidence.text: Gauging the flavor group shared by two chiral antisymmetric-tensor theories changes both their invariant coordinates and infrared Higgs sectors. The sextic interaction is supplied by the string construction and is the proposed ingredient that stabilizes the odd-M quantum runaway.

sources.title: Noninvertible Symmetries from Holography and Branes

evidence.text: Can holographic symmetry generators, including noninvertible defects, be extracted systematically from supergravity Gauss constraints and realized by D-brane worldvolume theories, with fusion and action on lines explained by brane dynamics?

sources.title: Branes and Non-Invertible Symmetries

evidence.text: Which objects in the IIB holographic dual represent non-invertible symmetries of N=4 theories with algebra so(4N), and how does their worldvolume dynamics produce the fusion rules?

sources.title: Back to heterotic strings on ALE spaces. Part I. Instantons, 2-groups and T-duality

evidence.text: Determine heterotic E8×E8 ALE-instanton little string theories with arbitrary asymptotic flat connections, identify candidate Spin(32)/Z2 T-duals, and investigate the R-symmetry 2-group constant as an RG monotone.

sources.title: Emergent supersymmetry at large N

evidence.text: Can matrix Gross–Neveu–Yukawa theories produce interacting infrared fixed points dominated by planar diagrams, with emergent supersymmetry or controlled non-supersymmetric sectors, and potentially interesting holographic duals?

sources.title: Disconnected gauge groups in the infrared

evidence.text: How does gauging charge conjugation modify the Seiberg–Witten geometry, Coulomb-branch singularities and massless BPS charges of higher-rank 4d N=2 SU(N) theories?

sources.title: SymTFT Fans: The symmetry theory of 4d $ \mathcal{N} $ = 4 super Yang-Mills on spaces with boundaries

evidence.text: How do Gaiotto–Witten boundary conditions modify the symmetry theory of 4d N=4 su(N) SYM, particularly its electric/magnetic 1-form symmetries and the transport of operators across boundary-associated sectors?

sources.title: Moduli space of $ \mathcal{N} $ = 4 super Yang-Mills from AdS/CFT

evidence.text: How do smooth holographic solitons encode vacuum selection and the supersymmetric solution space of strongly coupled N=4 SYM on a spatial circle, with two scalar-bilinear VEVs and three R-symmetry current sources?

sources.title: Chiral fermions from manifolds of G(2) holonomy

evidence.text: Construct and interpret additional conical G₂ singularities supporting four-dimensional chiral fermions, including examples with controlled matter physics but unknown metrics and examples with explicit metrics but less understood physics.

sources.title: Properties of some conformal field theories with M-theory duals

evidence.text: What central charges, wrapped-membrane chiral-primary data and charged-plasma properties can be extracted for four-dimensional N=1 SCFTs with supersymmetric AdS5 M-theory duals, and does the general solution class admit a consistent minimal five-dimensional truncation?

sources.title: Electric - magnetic duality, monopole condensation, and confinement in N=2 supersymmetric Yang-Mills theory

evidence.text: Determine the quantum vacuum geometry, BPS masses and strong-coupling behavior of pure N=2 SU(2) gauge theory, and explain confinement after an N=1 perturbation.

sources.title: A Strong coupling test of S duality

evidence.text: Can partition functions of topologically twisted N=4 Yang–Mills provide an exact strong-coupling test of Montonen–Olive duality in the vacuum with unbroken nonabelian gauge symmetry, through modular properties of instanton Euler-characteristic generating functions?

sources.title: M theory as a matrix model: A conjecture

evidence.text: Can uncompactified eleven-dimensional M-theory in the infinite-momentum frame be defined exactly by the large-N limit of D0-brane matrix quantum mechanics, reproducing supergravitons, their interactions, membranes and the required spacetime symmetries?

sources.title: RG fixed points in six-dimensions via branes at orbifold singularities

evidence.text: Which six-dimensional minimally supersymmetric gauge theories with tensor multiplets can support interacting RG fixed points, and can Type I D5 branes at orbifold singularities establish families of such theories?

sources.title: Rigid limit in N=2 supergravity and weak-gravity conjecture

evidence.text: Differentiate the microscopic prepotential, evaluate the inserted operator, and translate the coupling derivative to a scale derivative. This route determines the same type of relation without using the spectator-period Wronskian.

sources.title: Quantization of Integrable Systems and Four Dimensional Gauge Theories

evidence.text: Use QA-cohomology to represent supersymmetric vacua and the twisted chiral ring; use equivariant descent and the instanton partition function to compute the effective twisted superpotential.

sources.title: Holographic Duals of D=3 N=4 Superconformal Field Theories

evidence.text: Setting α=α̂=0 while retaining logarithmic five-brane sources removes the two asymptotic AdS₅×S⁵ regions. Local coordinate expansions establish smooth caps homeomorphic to AdS₄×B₆, locally AdS₄×R⁶.

sources.title: BPS Quivers and Spectra of Complete N=2 Quantum Field Theories

evidence.text: Glue quivers A and B using arrows only from A to B and choose arg Z(A)<arg Z(B). Mixed-support representations then have destabilizing B subrepresentations, leaving the union of the finite spectra. The quiver rule does not require completeness. Iterated augmented-triangulation gluing additionally requires a suitable chamber with no bound state using a chosen attachment node more than once.

sources.title: $\mathcal{N} = 2$ quantum field theories and their BPS quivers

evidence.text: For a left boundary crossing at node 1, mutate γ₁→−γ₁ and γⱼ→γⱼ+max(γⱼ◦γ₁,0)γ₁. Transform arrows and superpotential together, then integrate out opposite-arrow fields only when quadratic superpotential terms make them massive.

sources.title: Reading between the lines of four-dimensional gauge theories

evidence.text: Supersymmetric phase and duality arguments use N=2-to-N=1 mass deformations, monopole/dyon condensation, Higgsing, gaugino condensation and matching the area/perimeter behavior of lines across candidate dual descriptions.

sources.title: Categorical Equivalence and the Renormalization Group

evidence.text: How does renormalization group flow physically realize categorical or homotopy equivalences in presentations of stacks, derived categories and derived schemes, and what structures does this reveal on moduli spaces of SCFTs?

sources.title: More on 8D nonsupersymmetric branes and heterotic strings

evidence.text: Which maximal gauge enhancements and corresponding massless spectra arise in the nonsupersymmetric E8 heterotic string on T², and what codimension-two branes in supersymmetric heterotic theories would their discrete symmetries imply under quantum-gravity conjectures?

sources.title: Supersymmetric Janus Solutions in Four Dimensions

evidence.text: Construct supersymmetric conformal interfaces in the multiple-M2-brane theory using four-dimensional maximal gauged supergravity, including interfaces separating distinct superconformal fixed points.
